title: "one creator, truth is the name"

lines: A SEED THAT HOLDS A TREE.
cards: Describe God in a single breath. Not a book, not a sermon: a few words, short enough for a child to memorize and deep enough for a lifetime.
Right after the symbol for one, at the top of the scripture, Guru Nanak does exactly that. Sikhs call it the Mool Mantar, the root verse, and many say it every morning. Today, its first line.

teach.b: Mool means root. Mantar is the Punjabi form of mantra, a sacred phrase. The scripture's language is centuries old, and even fluent Punjabi speakers look words up, so one line at a time is how everyone reads it.
After Ik Onkar, it says: Sat Naam. Karta Purakh.
Sat means truth, and something deeper than true as opposed to false: it comes from an old root meaning what really is, what lasts.
Naam means name. Sat Naam: truth is the name, or the one whose name is truth.
The Victorian scholar Max Arthur Macauliffe, who translated with Sikh scholars beside him, gave the opening as: "There is but one God whose name is true, the Creator." Here's the surprise in naam.
On this path the name isn't just a label, like yours printed on a bill. It comes to mean the whole presence of God, running through everything.

teach.h: KARTA PURAKH — THE ONE STILL MAKING.
teach.b: Then Karta Purakh. Karta, the maker. Purakh, the being.
The creator: not a force that set the world going and walked away, but the one still making. Three ideas in five words: there is one, its name is truth, and it creates.
And a quiet challenge inside: if truth is God's name, then telling the truth is a way of saying it.

how: Sikhs recite the Mool Mantar at the start of the morning prayer Japji Sahib and at many other times; it stands at the head of the Guru Granth Sahib and is often the first passage children memorize.

games.q: what's inside the line — tap the pairs.
p: the name, and the presence of God

s: naam just means a label, like a name on a bill
on this path naam comes to mean the whole presence of God, running through everything.
the Mool Mantar begins with Ik Onkar
the root verse opens with the symbol for one, then Sat Naam, Karta Purakh.

"There is but one God whose name is true, the Creator."

games.q: you have one breath to describe God, right after the symbol for one. what comes next?
o: truth is the name; the creator.
games.why: Sat Naam, Karta Purakh: truth is the name, the creator. the root verse starts with what God is, not with rules.

practice: Breathe, and think of one true thing about your life right now: not the flattering version, just the true one. Sit with it without fixing it. If you like, let two words go out with the breath: Sat Naam.

wordCard.voice: The Mool Mantar, the root verse. Line one: Ik Onkar, Sat Naam, Karta Purakh. There is one, truth is the name, the creator. Tenth word.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: truth (sat) is the name (naam).

carryVoice: Your line: the name is truth. Which makes an honest sentence a small way of saying it. Day ten.
